$comment: Project-specific facts for the design-* skills, which live in ~/.claude/skills
and must not hard-code any one project. See CONTEXT.md for the domain language.

drift.$comment: Files that legitimately hold raw colour. Each needs a reason — an unexplained entry here is how a real drift gets buried.

why.public/mosaic-theme.js: the legacy runtime token source — superseded by tailwind.config.js, and a second palette definition is its own problem, not a drift finding
why.public/mobile/tokens.css: the mobile shell's own token file
why.public/guide-seed.js: printed Service Guide templates — a different medium with its own palette
why.public/relations-graph-core.js: the Relations Viewer group palette, documented in CONTEXT.md as deliberately raw

drift.$allow: Colours that must stay literal. Every entry needs a reason — this list is the difference between accounted for and stopped counting. Anything raw and not matched here fails --strict.

allow.why: the highlighter's pen colours. TipTap writes the value into the Note Body and renders it back wherever that note is read — including surfaces this stylesheet does not reach. The palette is declared as --highlight-* so a designer can see it; the code stores the number.
an inline trigger chip's colour, stored into the Note Body like a highlight. Declared as --chip-tag-added, --chip-tag-removed and --chip-status.
the fallback highlight for a note written before a colour was stored. Same reason as the pens.

the 'this page didn't finish loading' bar. If the page failed, mosaic.css may have failed with it — and a var() that resolves to nothing does not fall back, it removes the property. These literals are what make the error visible at all.
<meta name=theme-color>. The browser chrome reads it before any stylesheet, and var() is not honoured in a meta tag.

drift.$comment2: check finds, fix mends. fix is mechanical and reversible; it stops where judgement starts and lists what it left.

components.$comment: Today this shows only the verse picker. Growing it into every primitive as the app really draws them is what makes Pass 3 possible.
